novelty.justification: The claim's novelty route is a mechanism-guided adaptation method: it proposes that benign fine-tuning "perturbs the parameters supporting the refusal direction" and protects alignment by penalizing changes to "refusal-direction projections on a safety anchor set." Searches around "preserve refusal direction during fine-tuning," "safety subspace regularization LLM fine-tuning," and "interpretability-guided safety-preserving LoRA" identify SaLoRA (2025) as the closest prior method, while Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications (2024) and LoX (2025) already connect fine-tuning vulnerability to compact safety-critical parameter subspaces. Replacing those safety modules or low-rank regions with an interpretability-identified refusal subspace and preserving its activation projections is a non-trivial but natural extension and operationalization, rather than a new core relationship or intervention paradigm.
